11 Crash helmets
 
11.1 Tips for buying a crash helmet
Visors:
Visors are strongly recommended. However, it is important to ensure that these do not mist up; therefore, special covers are available that increase the anti-mist properties. When the helmet does not include eye protection it is highly recommended that safety glasses are used, although this use is not mandatory. Without eye protection, there is obviously the risk that something may enter the eye (an insect, a particle of sand or dust, etc.,) which may cause the rider to become distracted; however, the cold and/or the wind constantly in the eyes also increases visual fatigue.
(Página 82 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Safe driving  
 
11 The sun
The sun can cause dazzle and discomfort to the drivers of vehicles.
The suns rays directly (or indirectly) reflect off surfaces particularly shinny surfaces, such as windows, mirrors, cars etc. and also off of wet road surfaces.
In order to protect from this intense light and glare it is advisable to:
Keep all windows clean (refracted light can cause more discomfort).
Utilise the sun visor(s) and turn them to the most suitable angle.
Wear sunglasses (but only during the day and never at night or in tunnels.
(Página 233 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
12 Distances
 
12.5 Safety distance
The safety distance is the minimum space that a driver should leave between their vehicle and the vehicle ahead of them. This should be sufficient and enable them to stop, without impacting and colliding with the vehicle ahead of them, in the case of hard or unexpected braking by the preceding vehicle (the vehicle ahead of them). For safety it should always be greater than the stopping distance of the vehicle.
Not respecting the safety distance from the vehicle in front of you is the main cause of rear-end crashes.
This distance should be increased when travelling at higher speeds or in reduced visibility, or where the road has low adhesion qualities and when the driver is unsure of the locality or lacks experience.
Not maintaining the safety distance with the vehicle driving ahead of you can cost 4 points.
 
(Página 180 del manual 'Learning to drive')

4.4 Behaviour in the event of a burst tyre (blow out)
In case of a tyre blow out (rapid deflation of the tyre) the following action is necessary:
Stay calm.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, with two hands, to correct any change of course that may occur.
Smoothly maintain the pressure of the foot on the accelerator, then, raise it slowly (do not abruptly move your foot off the accelerator).
Use brakes sparingly. Attempt to reduce speed primarily by engine braking.

4 Wheels    
4.2 Tyres  
4.2.2 Tyre markings
The sides of the tyres contain information relating to their characteristics. The main ones are:
It is prohibited to mount tyres with a load index or a code below the speed of the tyres that were originally mounted on the vehicle or as recommended by the manufacturer. However, you can mount tyres that are greater than those recommended.
Type of tyres: At present, most tyres are tubeless.
Date of manufacture: Identifies the date of manufacture of the tyre by the use of four digits. The first two represent the week of the year and the last two the year of manufacture. For example, “1520” means week 15 (mid-April) of 2020. These figures may be within an oval.
Location indicator for wear: Tread wear indicators can be found within the grooves of the tyre. Tyre manufacturers mould tread wear indicators (T.W.I) into the design of the tyres tread pattern. This may be indicated by the symbol TWI (Tread Wear Indicator), or a triangle, arrow or other symbol indicated by the manufacturer.
(Página 69 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
2 Driver documentation              
           
2.4 Classes of driving permits        
2.4.5 B permit
With a B driving licence which is at least two years’ old, it is possible to drive, within the country, vehicles without trailers powered by alternative fuels for the transport of goods with a MAM above 3,500 kg but below 4,250 kg. This is provided that the mass above 3,500 kg is solely due to the propulsion system compared to the propulsion system of a vehicle with the same dimensions which is equipped with a standard internal combustion engine with spark or compression ignition, and provided that it does not increase the load capacity with regards to the same vehicle.
 
(Página 22 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
DISTRACTIONS
 
7 Smoking
Smoking, besides being harmful to health, affects driving because, amongst other factors, it causes distractions when searching and lighting the cigarette, makes one of the hands useless or generates vision problems due to smoke.
Smoking also causes excessive carbon monoxide to build up in the smoker’s body and therefore, alters the capabilities needed to drive safely causing a decrease in the level of attention needed at the wheel.
(Página 35 del manual 'Learning to drive')

DISTRACTIONS
 
7 Smoking
Drivers that smoke are involved in twice as many collisions than nonsmokers, usually because:
The entire process is a series of distractions; that is, finding the cigarette packet, removing it from within, lighting it, depositing the ash and extinguishing it.
It can lead to dangerous driving. Smokers tend to evaluate situations as less dangerous and take on more risks when driving.
(Página 35 del manual 'Learning to drive')

On interurban roads and main roads that do not have a pedestrian area, pedestrians will walk on the left-hand side in order to see the oncoming vehicles and to be warned of their presence, even though they are permitted to walk on the right when, for safety reasons, it is more suitable.

questions.help:
5 Generic speed        
     
5.3 Minimum generic speed
The generic minimum speed limits, both inside and outside populated areas, are:
On motorways and dual carriageways: 60 km/h for all motor vehicles.
On the remaining roads: the minimum speed is half of the maximum generic speed for each road.
(Página 174 del manual 'Learning to drive')

5 Generic speed    
 
5.3 Minimum generic speed
When you drive below these minimum limits you are said to travel at an abnormally reduced speed. This is considered an inadequate speed, as there is an increased risk of danger and a higher risk of a collision as a result of people overtaking the slower moving vehicles. It also adds to road congestion as it hampers the movement of other road users.
(Página 174 del manual 'Learning to drive')
